# Implementation Plan: crews `install-plugin` two-layer engine plugin provisioner (v3.14.0)
<!-- ralph-meta {"overviewTaskId":"crews-target-engine-plugin-provisioning"} -->

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-06-08. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph/jobs/crews-target-engine-plugin-provisioning/plan.md`.*

## Overview

Add an on-demand, lead/bookkeeper-invoked plugin installer to the **crews** plugin so a lead who notices a member's engine is missing a plugin (e.g. a codex member can't run `/plan-with-ralph` because only crews is installed in codex) can install/refresh it with a single command and get a clear, structured verdict telling them whether the blocked member must be respawned to actually see the new plugin.

The feature is a **two-layer surface**: (1) a tested crews CLI subcommand `install-plugin <plugin> --engine <copilot|claude|codex> [--version <v>] [--marketplace <name-or-localpath>] [--dry-run] [--exact]` that owns all install logic by thinly wrapping each engine's NATIVE plugin CLI and emits a structured JSON verdict; (2) a thin `/crews-install-plugin` skill (generated, not hand-written) that wraps the CLI; plus (3) a read-only discovery companion `list-plugins --engine <e>` that reports installed/enabled/version/source for crews / ralph-orchestration / ralph-overview. Durable logic lives in a tested `lib/plugin-provisioning/` library; the command modules and skills are thin. Ships as crews **3.13.0 → 3.14.0**.

The load-bearing feature is the **explicit restart/respawn verdict**: a freshly-installed plugin's skills/hooks only register in a FRESH engine thread, so the verdict carries `restartRequired` / `currentThreadUsable` and the human summary states the exact respawn action. Restart is **REPORT-ONLY** — the command never auto-restarts a running member.

## Research Findings

### Codebase Context
Source lives in the `ai-developer-toolkit` submodule at `plugins/crews/` (initialized in the PRIMARY codexu checkout, NOT in any plan worktree). crews is dependency-light CommonJS Node, no package-level `package.json`.

- **CLI dispatch**: `tools/crews.js` → `arm` to listener-loop, else `runCliCommand`. Registry-driven; the dispatcher needs NO change for new commands.
- **Command registry**: `hooks/commands/registry.js` — `COMMAND_DEFINITIONS` array of `{ name, aliases, load: () => require('./<name>') }`. Add new entries here.
- **Command runtime**: `hooks/commands/runtime.js` — `runCliCommand(name, argv, io, opts)` (help → parse → createContext → auth → handler → format → exit) and `dispatchSlashCommand`.
- **Command module shape** (exemplars `hooks/commands/list-members.js`, `inbox.js`, `spawn-member.js`): exports `{ name, aliases, description, usage, roleVisibility, surfaces: { slash:{enabled,auth,parseArgs,formatSuccess,formatError}, cli:{enabled,auth,usage,parseArgs,createContext,formatSuccess,formatError} }, handler }`. `handler(ctx,args)` returns a result object; `formatSuccess(result)` returns the stdout string. **JSON output** = `JSON.stringify(obj, null, 2)` (list-members.js:58-61; spawn-member CLI returns `{ ok, name, crew, pid, note }`).
- **Arg parsing**: `tools/lib/parse-crew-args.js::parseCrewArgs(argv, { flags })`. Errors: `CommandInputError` from `hooks/commands/errors.js` (re-exported by `helpers.js`).
- **Auth policies**: `hooks/commands/auth-policies.js`. Operator-trust pattern (spawn-member/stop-member): slash auth `active-lead-session`, cli auth `open` + `--as <lead>`. Read-only pattern (status/list-members): auth `open`/`any-actor`.
- **Engine awareness**: `hooks/actors.js` `VALID_ENGINES = ['claude','copilot','codex']` + `normalizeEngine()`; `hooks/lib/session-env.js::readSessionEnv()` 3-way tiebreak; `hooks/paths.js::getPluginRoot()` + home-path helpers.
- **Skills are GENERATED**: `scripts/gen-skills.js` reads `COMMANDS` from registry and writes `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (Claude) + `.copilot-plugin/copilot-skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (Copilot, kebab `/crews-<name>`) — header `<!-- GENERATED ... DO NOT HAND-EDIT -->`. Special sets: `NO_SKILL_COMMANDS`, `CLI_ONLY_MUTATING_COMMANDS`, `SLASH_ONLY_SKILL_COMMANDS`. Drift check: `node scripts/gen-skills.js --check`. `.codex-plugin/` ships ONE manifest + hooks only (NO per-skill files) → a new command needs only Claude+Copilot generated skills; it is still callable on a codex member via the UserPromptSubmit hook slash interception.
- **Version stamping**: `node plugins/crews/scripts/bump-version.js <x.y.z>` run from the **ai-developer-toolkit submodule root** writes 6 files (3 plugin manifests `.claude-plugin`/`.github/plugin`/`.codex-plugin` + 3 marketplace indexes) and the `const VERSION` literal in `tests/version.test.js`. `lib/version.js` reads `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` version. CHANGELOG.md gets a prepended `## 3.14.0 - <date>` entry.
- **Tests**: `tests/run.js` (fresh Worker per file, concurrency 10, serial denylist, per-worker temp HOME/USERPROFILE/CREWS_HOME + env scrub). Run `cd plugins/crews && node tests/run.js 2>&1 | tee <log>`. Helpers: `tests/lib/assert.js` (equal, ok), `tests/lib/repo-checks.js` (read). Typecheck (JS-only): `node --check <file.js>`. Pattern tests: `command-registry-shape.test.js`, `command-args-parity.test.js`, `version.test.js`.

### Native engine plugin CLIs (verified from local CLI help)
- **codex** — `codex plugin marketplace add <local-abs-path>`, `codex plugin add <plugin>@<marketplace>`, `codex plugin list`. **LOCAL-SOURCE ONLY**; git/URL source triggers the auto-upgrade marketplace-corruption bug (`.ralph/investigations/codex-git-marketplace-snapshot-tmp-ephemeral/findings.md`). Cache-lag is refreshed by re-running `codex plugin add` to recopy current source into a new cache version subdir (`.ralph/jobs/codex-engine-ralph-member-enablement/findings.md`). Cache: `~/.codex/plugins/cache/<mp>/<plugin>/<version>/`; config stanza: `~/.codex/config.toml`. **A live cache-lag case exists now**: source is 3.13.0 but local codex lists crews@ai-developer-toolkit at 3.12.1.
- **copilot** — `copilot plugin marketplace add <source>`, `copilot plugin install <plugin>@<marketplace>`, `copilot plugin list`. Install dir: `~/.copilot/installed-plugins/<mp>/<plugin>/` (single copy, no version subdir).
- **claude** — **native CLI DOES exist** (supersedes the brainstorm's "settings.json maybe" lean): `claude plugin marketplace add <source> --scope user`, `claude plugin install <plugin>@<marketplace> --scope user`, `claude plugin list --json`, `claude plugin enable`. Cache: `~/.claude/plugins/cache/<mp>/<plugin>/<version>/`; enablement in `~/.claude/settings.json` `enabledPlugins`. The native CLI is the PRIMARY claude adapter path; the direct `settings.json` edit is a documented FALLBACK only (used when `claude` CLI is not on PATH).

### Technical Constraints
- Per-engine home roots differ: `~/.codex`, `~/.copilot`, `~/.claude`. Resolve via the engine adapter, overridable for tests (injected home / env).
- Native `plugin list` text output is fragile to parse; prefer cache-dir + config cross-check for `installedVersion`/`enabled` where possible. `claude plugin list --json` is structured → use it.
- Non-interactive invocation: use argv arrays with `spawnSync`/`execFileSync` (NOT shell strings). Inject the command runner so tests never spawn a real `codex`/`copilot`/`claude`.
- This is a SUBMODULE task: two-commit flow (commit crews submodule first, then codexu pointer bump — LEAD owns the pointer bump + wrapper ceremony). Impl member commits on a topic branch in a **submodule worktree** and must NOT edit codexu root `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` or the parent submodule pointer.

## Approach

### Architecture
A pure, unit-testable provisioning library plus two thin command modules:

```
plugins/crews/lib/plugin-provisioning/
  index.js          # orchestrator: installPlugin(opts), listPlugins(opts), buildVerdict(...)
  version.js        # semver parse + compare (crews has NO reusable semver helper) — pure
  source.js         # resolve (a) marketplace source: explicit --marketplace (name|abs-path)
                    #   > already-registered engine marketplace > default <repo>/ai-developer-toolkit,
                    #   AND (b) plugin NAME -> source dir via the marketplace index `plugins[].source`
                    #   (e.g. ralph-orchestration -> ./plugins/ralph; name != dir). sourceVersion reads
                    #   from <resolved-source-dir>/.claude-plugin/plugin.json, NOT <toolkit>/plugins/<name>
  command-runner.js # injectable runner seam (default execFileSync; tests inject a fake)
  adapters/
    codex.js        # detectState / installOrUpgrade (local-source only, cache-lag refresh) / verify
    copilot.js      # detectState / installOrUpgrade / verify
    claude.js       # detectState (claude plugin list --json; handles user+project SCOPE & duplicates) /
                    #   installOrUpgrade (native CLI `--scope user`; settings.json fallback ENABLES an
                    #   already-cached version only -- it cannot populate the cache) / verify

plugins/crews/hooks/commands/
  install-plugin.js # require --engine; <plugin> positional; --version/--marketplace/--dry-run/--exact
  list-plugins.js   # require --engine; read-only discovery over crews/ralph-orchestration/ralph-overview
```

**Adapter contract** (each of codex/copilot/claude exports the same 3 functions, plus an injected `run`, `homeDir`):
- `detectCurrentState({ plugin, marketplaceSource, run, homeDir })` → `{ installed, installedVersion, enabled, installPath, marketplaceSource, marketplaceRegistered }`.
- `installOrUpgrade({ plugin, marketplaceSource, requiredVersion, exact, sourcePath, run, homeDir })` → performs idempotent native-CLI install/upgrade (codex also handles cache-lag refresh); returns the post-action detected state. Refuses git/URL marketplace for codex with an actionable error citing the corruption bug.
- `verify({ plugin, installPath, expectedVersion, run, homeDir })` → cross-checks cache/install dir + config/list; returns `{ verified, installedVersion, enabled }`.

**Orchestrator** (`index.js`):
- `installPlugin(opts)`: resolve source → `detectCurrentState` → compute action (no-op vs install vs upgrade using `version.js` against the source version; default `--version` = MINIMUM-ACCEPTABLE so installed ≥ required = no-op; `--exact` forces exact match) → if mutate, call `installOrUpgrade` then `verify` → assemble verdict. On any thrown adapter error, return `status:"failed"` with an actionable (non-opaque) message and the partial-state note (see Failure handling).
- `listPlugins(opts)`: for each of `['crews','ralph-orchestration','ralph-overview']`, resolve the source dir via the marketplace index (`source.js` — ralph-orchestration → `plugins/ralph`), run the adapter `detectCurrentState` + read `<resolved-source-dir>/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` version → report `{ plugin, installed, enabled, installedVersion, sourceVersion, marketplaceSource, installPath }`.
- `buildVerdict`: assemble `{ status, plugin, engine, scope?, installedVersion, sourceVersion, requiredVersion, enabled, installPath, marketplaceSource, restartRequired, currentThreadUsable, summary, error? }`. Restart/usability are derived PER STATUS (NOT the naive `currentThreadUsable = !restartRequired`, which would wrongly report a failed install as usable):

  | status | restartRequired | currentThreadUsable |
  |---|---|---|
  | `no-op` | false | true (already installed+enabled; nothing changed) |
  | `installed` / `upgraded` | true | false (a FRESH engine thread is required to see new skills/hooks) |
  | `failed` | false (a restart will not help — nothing was installed) | reflects the PRE-action state: `true` ONLY if the plugin was already installed+enabled before the failed attempt, else `false` |

  The `summary` states the exact respawn action when `restartRequired`, e.g. *"crews installed into codex at 3.14.0. The currently-running codex member cannot see new skills until it is respawned in a FRESH codex thread — stop and re-spawn the member."* On `failed`, the summary states the actionable error and that no respawn will help until the install succeeds.

## Scope

### In Scope
- Two-layer surface: `install-plugin` CLI subcommand (structured JSON verdict) + generated thin skill, plus `list-plugins` read-only discovery command + generated skill.
- All three engine adapters, each a thin wrapper over the engine's NATIVE plugin CLI (codex local-source-only + cache-lag refresh; copilot native; claude native CLI primary with `--scope user`, handling the user-vs-project scope + duplicate-list case; the claude settings.json fallback ENABLES an already-cached version only).
- Plugin-name → source-dir resolution via the marketplace index `plugins[].source` (name != dir; e.g. `ralph-orchestration` → `plugins/ralph`).
- Idempotency: no-op (installed ≥ required) vs install vs upgrade; `--version` defaults to minimum-acceptable; `--exact` opt-in. A local-source marketplace exposes exactly ONE version (the checkout's): an `--exact <v>` whose `v` differs from `sourceVersion` and is not already installed returns `status:"failed"` with an actionable message (local source cannot materialize an arbitrary exact version).
- `install-plugin` is a MUTATING lead command — handler-side enforces lead authorization (in-session lead auto-resolve, or `--as <lead>` / `resolveActorRole(...) === 'lead'` for external orchestrators), matching `spawn-member`/`stop-member`.
- Explicit REPORT-ONLY restart/respawn verdict (`restartRequired`/`currentThreadUsable` + human summary with the exact respawn action).
- Discovery surface: `install-plugin --dry-run` (single-plugin preview, no mutation) AND standalone `list-plugins --engine <e>` (multi-plugin report over crews / ralph-orchestration / ralph-overview).
- `--engine` REQUIRED (no silent caller-default).
- Failure: `status:"failed"` with actionable non-opaque error; documents partial marketplace-registration state rather than rolling back a shared marketplace.
- Tests for the provisioning lib + version-bump; crews `3.13.0 → 3.14.0`; CHANGELOG + AGENTS.md updated.

### Out of Scope (note as FUTURE)
- Auto-provision-on-spawn hook (design lib so a future spawn-time hook can reuse `installPlugin`, but do not build the hook).
- `--respawn-member <name>` follow-up (keep restart report-only; future opt-in).
- `--verify-skills` that boots a fresh engine session to confirm skills register (v1 verifies install-state via list + cache + config cross-check only).
- Direct config/cache reconciler as the DEFAULT path (only the narrow, clearly-labelled claude settings.json fallback is sanctioned).
- Codex-skill discoverability for the new command (would require a `.codex-plugin` skills overlay; the command is already callable on codex via the UserPromptSubmit hook).

## Risk Areas
- **Native CLI output drift** — parsing `codex/copilot plugin list` text is fragile. Mitigation: prefer cache-dir + config cross-check; use `claude plugin list --json`; keep parsers small + unit-tested against committed fixture strings.
- **Codex cache-lag refresh correctness** — the re-run-`codex plugin add` refresh must produce a new cache version subdir matching source version. Mitigation: dedicated unit test with a fake `~/.codex` tree; manual smoke against the live 3.12.1→3.13.0 lag.
- **`--engine` cross-engine footgun** — installing into the wrong engine. Mitigation: require `--engine`, echo the resolved engine in the verdict + summary.
- **Same-plugin parallel conflict** — `install-plugin` and `list-plugins` both touch `registry.js` and the generated skills dir; run `gen-skills.js` once after both are registered. This is ONE ralph job (serial stories), not parallel jobs.
- **Partial-state on failure** — a registered-but-install-failed marketplace is shared; rolling it back could break other plugins. Mitigation: document the partial state in the error, do not roll back the shared marketplace.
- **Claude install scope** — `claude plugin list --json` returns entries across BOTH `user` and `project` scopes (this box already shows a duplicate for `crews@ai-developer-toolkit`). Installing `--scope user` may NOT fix a stale project-scoped install for the current workspace. Mitigation: default `--scope user`, report the resolved `scope` in the verdict, detect+surface a conflicting project-scoped entry, and unit-test the duplicate-list case.
- **Plugin name ≠ directory** — `ralph-orchestration` lives at `plugins/ralph`. Mitigation: resolve source dirs via the marketplace `plugins[].source` field, never `<toolkit>/plugins/<name>`; unit-test the ralph-orchestration case.
- **Auth (decided)** — install-plugin = operator-trust (lead, enforced handler-side), list-plugins = read-only (open). See Open Questions for the exact tags + the generated-skill shape.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC1 (idempotent no-op): running `install-plugin` for an already-correctly-installed plugin returns `status:"no-op"`, `restartRequired:false`, `currentThreadUsable:true`, and makes NO changes — verified by unchanged cache/config + the adapter `detectCurrentState` before/after being equal. Verified in `plugin-provisioning-orchestrator.test.js` with an injected runner whose detect reports installed ≥ required.
- AC2 (codex install + restart verdict): installing `ralph-orchestration` into codex via the local-source marketplace yields a verdict `status:"installed"` (or `"upgraded"`), `restartRequired:true`, `currentThreadUsable:false`, with a summary containing an explicit "spawn a fresh codex thread/member" instruction; the codex adapter calls `codex plugin marketplace add <local-abs-path>` then `codex plugin add ralph-orchestration@<mp>` (argv asserted on the injected runner); the `ralph-orchestration` source dir is resolved via the marketplace index to `plugins/ralph` (name ≠ dir). Verified in `plugin-provisioning-codex.test.js`.
- AC3 (codex git-source refusal): a codex install with a git/URL `--marketplace` returns `status:"failed"` with an error message that cites the auto-upgrade corruption bug and registers NO marketplace (the injected runner records ZERO `marketplace add` calls). Verified in `plugin-provisioning-codex.test.js`.
- AC4 (codex cache-lag refresh): given a fake `~/.codex` where `plugin list`/cache reports an installed version LOWER than the source version, the codex adapter re-runs `codex plugin add` so the post-action `installedVersion` equals `sourceVersion`, verified via the cache version subdir + the recorded `plugin add` call. Verified in `plugin-provisioning-codex.test.js`.
- AC5 (copilot path): the copilot adapter installs/updates via `copilot plugin install <plugin>@<mp>` (argv asserted) and verifies via `copilot plugin list` + the single-copy install dir `~/.copilot/installed-plugins/<mp>/<plugin>/`. Verified in `plugin-provisioning-copilot.test.js`.
- AC6 (claude native CLI + scope): the claude adapter installs via `claude plugin install <plugin>@<mp> --scope user` + `claude plugin enable` and detects state via `claude plugin list --json`, correctly handling output that lists the SAME plugin under both `user` and `project` scopes (it keys on the `user` scope and surfaces a conflicting project-scoped entry rather than mis-reporting); the verdict carries the resolved `scope`. When the `claude` CLI is absent (injected runner throws ENOENT): if the target version is ALREADY cached, the adapter enables it via the `~/.claude/settings.json` `enabledPlugins` edit (the fallback ENABLES only — it cannot populate the cache); if it is NOT cached, the adapter returns `status:"failed"` with an actionable "claude CLI required to install/populate cache" message. Verified in `plugin-provisioning-claude.test.js` (duplicate-scope list, enable-from-cache fallback, and no-cache failure).
- AC7 (discovery surface): `list-plugins --engine <e>` reports, for each of crews / ralph-orchestration / ralph-overview: `installed`, `enabled`, `installedVersion`, `sourceVersion`, `marketplaceSource`, `installPath` (JSON). `sourceVersion` for `ralph-orchestration` MUST be read from `plugins/ralph/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` resolved through the marketplace `source` field (NOT a naive `plugins/ralph-orchestration` path). Verified in `list-plugins-command.test.js` (mocked adapters) + a `plugin-provisioning-source.test.js` case asserting the ralph-orchestration name→dir resolution.
- AC8 (failed install is actionable + does not imply usability): a failed install returns `status:"failed"` with a non-opaque error (not a raw CLI dump), the verdict documents any partial marketplace-registration state instead of silently leaving it, AND `currentThreadUsable` is NOT forced to `true` — it is `false` when the plugin was not already installed+enabled before the attempt (a failed install never claims the current thread can use the plugin), and `restartRequired` is `false`. Verified in `plugin-provisioning-orchestrator.test.js`.
- AC9 (`--engine` required + `--dry-run`): `install-plugin` without `--engine` errors with usage; `--dry-run` computes and returns the verdict WITHOUT calling any mutating adapter method (injected runner records ZERO `marketplace add` / `plugin add|install|enable` calls). The dry-run verdict reuses the same `status` enum reflecting the would-be action (`no-op` / `installed` / `upgraded`) plus `dryRun:true`, with `restartRequired`/`currentThreadUsable` computed as if applied and the `summary` phrased "would install/upgrade …". Verified in `install-plugin-command.test.js`.
- AC10 (registry + skills + version): `install-plugin` and `list-plugins` appear in `command-registry-shape.test.js`/`command-args-parity.test.js`; `node scripts/gen-skills.js --check` reports no drift after regeneration; `tests/version.test.js` asserts crews `3.14.0` across all 6 files; `node --check` passes on every new/changed `.js`; full `node tests/run.js` is green.
- AC11 (`--exact` impossible case): an `install-plugin <p> --engine <e> --exact <v>` where `<v>` differs from the local-source `sourceVersion` AND the plugin is not already installed at `<v>` returns `status:"failed"` with an actionable message naming `sourceVersion` and explaining a local-source marketplace cannot materialize an arbitrary exact version (no mutating call is made). Verified in `plugin-provisioning-orchestrator.test.js`.
- AC12 (mutating-command auth): the `install-plugin` slash path rejects a non-lead session, and the CLI path requires `--as <lead>` (or in-session lead auto-resolve) — a missing/invalid lead is rejected with an actionable error; `list-plugins` (read-only) is callable by member or lead. Verified in `install-plugin-command.test.js` (non-lead + missing-`--as` rejection) and `list-plugins-command.test.js`.
- AC13 (gated live smoke): a `CREWS_PROVISIONING_LIVE=1`-gated smoke runs `list-plugins --engine <caller-engine>` (read-only) and an `install-plugin --dry-run` against the REAL engine CLI and asserts the JSON verdict shape (catches native-CLI output drift the injected-runner unit tests cannot). Skipped by default in `tests/run.js`. Documented in the test file header.

## Suggested Decomposition
All stories live in the SAME repo (the crews submodule) and share load-bearing files — `registry.js` (US-006/US-007), the generated skills dir (US-007), and the 6 version stamps + CHANGELOG + AGENTS.md (US-008). Per the codexu AGENTS.md "same-plugin parallel = conflict; must serialize" rule, this is a SINGLE serial cluster executed in dependency order within one Ralph job. There is no parallel-job decomposition.

- Stories: US-001, US-002, US-003, US-004, US-005, US-006, US-007, US-008

- **Auth tags** (decided; confirm only the member-callable relaxation): `install-plugin` is operator/lead-driven and MUTATING → roleVisibility `['lead']`, slash auth `active-lead-session`, cli auth `open` with handler-side lead enforcement (in-session lead auto-resolve, or `--as <lead>` for external orchestrators), matching the spawn-member/stop-member operator-trust pattern. NOTE (corrects an initial-review false positive): operator-trust commands do NOT generate a "slash-only" skill — per the real `skills/stop-member/SKILL.md`, gen-skills emits a CLI-wrapping body (`node $CREWS_BIN install-plugin …`) with an `--as <lead>`/in-session-auto-resolve callout, because `skillFallbackProse` gates only on `!cliEnabled || SLASH_ONLY_SKILL_COMMANDS`, NOT on operator-trust. Confirm only whether `install-plugin` should ALSO be member-callable (relax to `open`).
- **`list-plugins` vs `install-plugin --status`** — plan ships BOTH a standalone `list-plugins` (multi-plugin discovery, matches AC7's per-engine 3-plugin report) and `install-plugin --dry-run` (single-plugin preview). If the operator wants only one surface, drop `list-plugins` and add a `--status` flag — but the 3-plugin discovery report maps more cleanly to a standalone command.
- **`source.js` default marketplace path** — defaults to the local `ai-developer-toolkit` checkout. Marketplace resolution order: explicit `--marketplace` (name or abs-path) > already-registered engine marketplace of that name > the toolkit root resolved by walking up from the crews plugin root (`hooks/paths.js::getPluginRoot()` → up to `<toolkit>`). Confirm the walk-up heuristic at impl. SEPARATELY, plugin-name → source-dir resolution always reads the marketplace index `plugins[].source` (handles `ralph-orchestration` → `plugins/ralph`).
